title: Fast Virtual Gate Extraction For Silicon Quantum Dot Devices
problem: Controlling silicon quantum dot arrays requires establishing orthogonal potential control on individual dots. Conventional virtual gate extraction methods involve high experimental overhead, limiting practical scaling.
motivation: Silicon quantum dot devices promise large-scale quantum computing with extended coherence times and compact size, but efficient device control is essential for scalability.
method: Instead of testing every voltage combination (which is experimentally expensive and impractical), the method focuses on the voltage ranges where quantum dots transition between different charge states. It uses efficient voltage sweeping to pinpoint these transition boundaries and filters out measurement errors. This targeted approach requires far fewer experiments because it measures only the critical operating regions where independent dot control is established, rather than mapping the entire voltage space.
key_novelty: The key insight is that establishing independent quantum dot control only requires measuring where dots change their charge state, not scanning every possible voltage combination.
contributions: Device physics-guided virtual gate extraction method for quantum dot control
Efficient voltage sweeping strategy targeting charge state transitions
5.84× to 19.34× speedup demonstration on real quantum dot chips
primary_theme: Accelerating quantum dot device calibration via targeted gate extraction
